page: The Amazon Web Services c7i-flex.8xlarge is a 7th-generation compute-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro System. Its hardware specification includes 32 vCPUs across 16 physical cores with 2 threads per core, powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8488C processor running at a base clock speed of 3.2 GHz. Cache architecture consists of 48 KB L1d cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 105 MB L3 cache. It is provisioned with 64.0 GB of DDR5 memory clocked at 5 GHz, yielding 2.0 GB of memory per vCPU. Hardware instruction extensions include AVX-512, AMX Tile/INT8, VAES, and SHA_NI. The system has a baseline network bandwidth of 6 Gbps, includes zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses, and features no integrated local storage or dedicated GPUs.

Benchmark evaluation highlights notable single-threaded compute efficiency. In Geekbench single-core testing, the instance achieved a score of 2074.0, while single-threaded gzip compression reached 33.6 GB/sec and bzip3 decompression achieved 13.85 GB/sec, placing all three in top-tier performance brackets. PassMark encryption testing recorded 35,678.6, and static web serving throughput reached 51.12 GB/sec. In multi-core workloads, stress-ng multi-core CPU score registered 35,034.78 and Geekbench multi-core hit 15,951.0, both settling in average benchmark tiers. Small LLM model (135M) generation reached 286.26 tokens/sec, whereas 7B model generation measured 18.95 tokens/sec.

Given its burstable CPU allocation profile, the c7i-flex.8xlarge delivers qualitative cost efficiency for workloads with fluctuating execution demands or intermittent idle periods rather than continuous maximum resource utilization. The 1:2 RAM-to-vCPU ratio and high single-threaded instruction throughput suit applications such as static web serving, software build compilation, batch data compression, and lightweight LLM text generation. Workloads requiring sustained continuous 100% CPU utilization, persistent local disk IOPS, or large-model GPU acceleration will require alternative instance classes.
